t.7.39.1: While the bears, monkeys and rākṣasas were thus dwelling there, Rāghava of great splendour spoke these words to Sugrīva.
t.7.39.3: O mighty-armed one, filled with the highest affection, look upon Aṅgada, and Hanumān, and Nala of exceedingly great strength.
t.7.39.2: Go now, gentle one, to Kiṣkindhā, which cannot be assailed by gods or asuras, and together with your ministers rule the kingdom, now cleared of every thorn.
t.7.39.4: Suṣeṇa, the heroic father-in-law, and Tāra, foremost among the mighty, and the unassailable Kumuda, and Nīla of exceedingly great strength.
t.7.39.5: The heroic Śatabali, and Mainda and Dvivida as well, Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, and the mighty Śarabha.
t.7.39.6: And behold, filled with affection, the invincible king of the bears, the mighty Jāmbavant, and Gandhamādana as well.
t.7.39.7: And these other exceedingly great-souled ones, who were ready to give up their lives for my sake, look upon them with affection, and never do anything displeasing to them.
t.7.39.8: Having spoken thus to Sugrīva and praised him again and again, Rāma then addressed Vibhīṣaṇa in a sweet voice.
t.7.39.9: Rule Laṅkā according to dharma, O king, for you are held in esteem by the city, by the Rākṣasas, and by your brother Vaiśravaṇa.
t.7.39.11: And I, together with Sugrīva, should always be remembered by you, O king, with the greatest affection; go now, free from distress.
t.7.39.10: And never, O king, set your mind on unrighteousness in any way, for kings who are wise surely enjoy the earth.
t.7.39.12: Having heard the words of Rāma, the bears, monkeys and rākṣasas praised Kākutstha again and again, crying, "Well done, well done!"
t.7.39.13: O mighty-armed Rāma, your intellect, your truly wondrous valor, and your supreme sweetness are always like those of Svayambhū.
t.7.39.14: While the vānaras and rākṣasas were speaking thus, Hanūmān, bowing low, addressed these words to Rāghava.
t.7.39.15: O king, my supreme affection is ever established in you, and my devotion is steadfast, O hero; my heart goes nowhere else.
t.7.39.16: O hero, as long as I shall hear the story of Rāma upon the face of the earth, so long may my life-breaths remain in my body; of this there is no doubt.
t.7.39.17: Then, as Hanūmān was speaking thus, the king of kings rose from his seat, embraced him, and spoke these words.
t.7.39.18: So shall it be, O best of monkeys; there is no doubt of this. For as long as the worlds endure, so long shall my story endure.
t.7.39.19: For as long as this story of mine shall travel through the worlds, so long shall your life-breaths dwell in your body; of this there is no doubt.
t.7.39.20: Then Rāghava, out of affection, loosened from his own neck a necklace bright as the moon, with a beryl as its central gem, and fastened it upon Hanumān.
t.7.39.21: With that necklace bound upon his chest, the great monkey shone like the lord of golden mountains whose summit is overspread by the moon.
t.7.39.22: Having heard these words of Rāghava, the mighty vānaras rose up one after another, bowed their heads to his feet, and departed.
t.7.39.23: Mighty-armed Sugrīva was embraced by Rāma, and so too was Vibhīṣaṇa, whose soul was devoted to dharma, clasped closely to his breast.
t.7.39.24: And all of them, their throats choked with tears and their eyes brimming, senseless and as though bewildered by grief, then took leave of Rāghava.
